summary: Access control is confirmed obfuscation not encryption (static salt + public passcodes); Master tier is fully bypassable client-side with zero credentials via 2 independent paths, VIP allowlist manager is non-functional across browsers and has an unescaped-innerHTML XSS bug.
result_text: TRACK 1 — access.js (866 lines) + README "Multi-Tier Access Control" section Verified against live repo @ commit matching graphify HEAD 13d686ad (community 75, 30 nodes, cohesion 0.12 — confirmed). ## Core verdict (task's central question) "Zero-Leak" is real for ciphertext-at-rest (no visitor ever sees gated HTML unencrypted in page source) but the *access control* itself is 100% obfuscation, not a security boundary. Every input to key derivation ships in plaintext JS: static PBKDF2 salt `'adt_salt_2026'` (access.js:56), VIP passcode `'vip2026'` (also printed directly in the unlock-modal DOM for all visitors, access.js:580-582 — an intentional "recruiter gimmick" per dev-logs v-history, so no action needed there), and Master passcode `'master2026'` hardcoded as a fallback constant (access.js:405, 427, 521) — never entered by a user anywhere, never fetched from a server. Anyone reading script.js can derive both AES keys offline with zero interaction with the UI. Severity by tier: LOW for VIP — already publicly framed as a non-secret demo gate, protects nothing sensitive (project descriptions, extended repo links). MEDIUM-HIGH for Master — README explicitly claims it's "exclusively via Google Sign-In," and dev-logs (line 219) previously concluded the scheme was "confirmed legitimate ... real Google Sign-In, Master gated to 4 owner Gmail addresses." That conclusion is wrong: see H1/H2 below, both independently confirmed by reading the code, no execution needed. ## HIGH H1 — access.js:401-405, 521, 806-812: Master tier is achievable with **zero credentials** via the app's own public API: `ACCESS_CONTROL.setSimulatedTier(2)` (or clicking the "Master" sim button, which is only UI-hidden, not permission-checked at the function level) sets `getEffectiveTier()` to TIER_MASTER. `updateGatedContentVisibility()` then falls back to the hardcoded `'master2026'` passcode to decrypt the real Master ciphertext — no session, no sign-in, no passcode entry. Equivalent one-liner from devtools: `localStorage.setItem('adt_access_session', JSON.stringify({tier:2}))` then `ACCESS_CONTROL.updateUI()`. `getSessionData()`/`getActualTier()` (access.js:96-107) do zero integrity/signature validation on the stored session — it's trusted as-is. Fix: none possible client-side without a backend; at minimum stop treating Master as a real security boundary in docs/copy. H2 — access.js:171-186 (`parseJwt`) + 229-278 (`handleGoogleCredentialResponse`): The Google ID token (JWT) is base64-decoded for its payload only — **no signature verification** against Google's public keys (no call to Google's tokeninfo endpoint or JWKS). `handleGoogleCredentialResponse` is assigned to `window.handleGoogleCredentialResponse` (line 325) and is also directly callable as a bare global function. A self-crafted, unsigned "JWT-shaped" string (`header.base64({"email":"aaradhyadevtmr@gmail.com"}).sig`) passed to it produces a real `saveGoogleSession(TIER_MASTER, 'master2026', {...})` — going through the *intended* "Sign in with Google" code path with a fully spoofed identity, no Google account or OAuth handshake involved at all. Fix: same as H1 — structurally unfixable without a server to verify the token; the honest framing is "Master tier is a UI convenience for the owner, not an access boundary." H3 — access.js:196-220 (`addCustomVipEmail`/`removeCustomVipEmail`): No tier/permission check inside the functions themselves (contrast `promptForGoogleClientId`, access.js:285-288, which does check `getEffectiveTier() !== TIER_MASTER`). Any visitor can call `addCustomVipEmail('x@y.com')` from devtools directly — bypassing the "Master Admin control panel" framing entirely. Low practical impact today only because `vipEmails: ['*']` (core.js:20) already grants VIP to any Google sign-in, so this allowlist is currently redundant — but the code path itself has no authorization check and would be a real bypass the moment the wildcard is narrowed. ## MEDIUM M1 — access.js:188-220, `adt_custom_vip_emails` key: The "live VIP allowlist manager" is a functional no-op for its README-stated purpose ("Master Admin control panel features a live allowlist manager widget to add/remove custom VIP user emails dynamically"). It writes to `localStorage` on whichever browser clicks the button — there is no backend/sync, so an email added by the owner on their own machine never grants VIP to that email on any other visitor's browser. Should be documented as "local browser only" or removed/reframed. M2 — assets/js/modules/access.js:848-853 (`renderMasterControlPanel`'s VIP list render): `vipWrap.innerHTML = customList.map(email => ...${email}...).join('')` interpolates the stored email string directly into `innerHTML` with no escaping. `addCustomVipEmail`'s only validation is `.includes('@')` (access.js:198), so a string like `@x` passes validation and stored HTML executes on next panel render. Exploitation is currently self-XSS only (localStorage is same-origin, no cross-origin write vector found), but it's a real missing-escaping bug independent of that — fix with `textContent` or HTML-escaping before interpolation. M3 — core.js:20 `vipEmails: ['*']` vs README:84 "Google Sign-In with an authorized email/domain": the README implies a restricted allowlist; in reality *any* verified Google account instantly gets VIP. Not a bug (comment at core.js:20 documents the wildcard intentionally) but the README's security framing overstates the restriction — worth a doc fix, not a code fix. M4 — index.html:1145 `#master-exclusive` section has no default `display:none` in CSS (checked assets/css/style.css:1071 — only padding/layout rules, no visibility rule); it's hidden exclusively by JS (`updateGatedContentVisibility`) at runtime, and the lock overlay is also JS-injected. If the dynamically-loaded module script (assets/js/script.js:7-30, injected via `createElement('script')`) fails to load — network hiccup, ad/script blocker, no-JS — the section renders with its title ("System Diagnostics & Master Console") and an empty card, visible to all, with no overlay explaining the gate. Contradicts the "hidden from public guests" / "Zero Raw HTML Leakage" framing (README:89,92) — fails open, not closed. Low actual leak (title only, no ciphertext/content), but inconsistent with the stated design. M5 — core.js:16-19: `masterEmails` hardcodes 4 personal Gmail addresses in cleartext (`aaradhyadevtmr@gmail.com`, `aaradhya.bei79001@gmail.com`, `adtgames2061@gmail.com`, `devtamrakaraaradhya83@gmail.com`) — README only documents one. Anyone reading the JS gets 3 additional personal addresses not otherwise advertised. Not an access-control issue, but a personal-info exposure worth a conscious call (intentional convenience vs. minor privacy leak). ## LOW L1 — access.js:56-73 (`getDecryptionKey`): re-runs the full 100k-iteration PBKDF2-SHA256 derivation on *every* `decryptHexPayload()` call instead of memoizing per-passcode. On `projects.html` (~22 VIP-tier `proj-*` links, access.js:420-462 loop) this is ~22 redundant full derivations per page load or tier-change event. Pure perf waste, not a security concern — cache the derived `CryptoKey` per passcode. L2 — access.js:118 `VIP_PASSCODES: ['vip2026', 'vip', 'tier1']`: two undocumented aliases beyond the one shown in the UI/README. No security implication (all three are equally public), just dead trivia/confusion risk. L3 — access.js:129-136, 140-151 (`saveSession`/`saveGoogleSession`): session object (incl. Google profile name/email/picture for Google sign-ins) persists in `localStorage` indefinitely with no TTL/expiry — only cleared via explicit "Lock Session" click. Minor persistence-on-shared-machine concern for a portfolio demo; low real risk given no sensitive data is actually gated. ## NIT N1 — dev-logs/PortfolioWebsite_TRACKER.md:219,242,271 already tracked and resolved the one prior known issue in this module (orphaned `achievements-vip` payload key) — re-verified clean: 25 payload keys in `ACCESS_CONTROL_PAYLOADS`, 25 matching `data-payload-id`/`data-payload-link-id` references across index.html/projects.html, zero orphans, zero unresolved references. No action needed, confirming for the record only. ## Not re-flagged (per scope) Did not re-check id/href integrity, tag balance, JS syntax, or global ID uniqueness — covered by verify.py's 17 automated checks per task instructions.
